answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 45% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the horizon ordering is published with the walnut batch, the plume audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early hence gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 306 account operation therefore ties up 32 million dollars of idle capital. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
